name: Dead Kennedys
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: A San Francisco punk band that ran its own label, got a poster prosecuted in Los Angeles, and then spent a quarter century in court over who owns its songs.

eras.title: An ad in The Recycler, and a name nobody wanted to print
eras.text: East Bay Ray placed a musician's ad in June 1978, and by July the band was opening at the Mabuhay Gardens. By the end of the year a Chronicle columnist was complaining about the name, and by the end of 1979 the singer had run for mayor.

years.h: [[East Bay Ray|d8559d8b-a8ee-4174-b5f1-226fe5e2891a]] answers his own ad, and a band shows up
years.p: Ray, who'd played rockabilly in a band called Cruis'n, advertised in The Recycler. Bassist Klaus Flouride answered; singer Jello Biafra, drummer Ted and guitarist 6025 filled out the first lineup.

years.cap: Mabuhay Gardens, San Francisco. Photo/flyer needed.
years.h: First show: Mabuhay Gardens, opening for DV8 and Negative Trend
years.p: The Offs headlined the July 19, 1978 bill. The band went on under its own name, but Ray says the name was never meant as an insult to the Kennedy family.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the band played early gigs under aliases including the DK's, the Sharks, the Creamsicles and the Pink Twinkies, because the name was drawing complaints. Ray has said the name stood for the assassinations of John F. Kennedy, Martin Luther King Jr. and Robert F. Kennedy as the killing of the American Dream.

In November 1978 San Francisco Chronicle columnist Herb Caen wrote about the band's tastelessness, noting a booking on November 22, the 15th anniversary of the JFK assassination. Per Wikipedia, the Mabuhay's owner refused to cancel because of an existing contract.

years.src: Wikipedia: Carlo Cadona · Wikipedia: Live at the Deaf Club
years.h: Guitarist 6025 plays his last show, at the Deaf Club
years.p: Carlo Cadona had co-written songs like "Forward to Death" and "Ill in the Head" before leaving in March 1979. The tape sat unreleased for 25 years.
years.xp:
Cadona joined a week before the first gig, according to Biafra, and Biafra later called him "the best all-around musician in the band." Biafra has said 6025's prog-rock leanings and unusual songwriting created friction with the rest of the band.

The March 3, 1979 set, with original drummer Ted on the kit, finally came out as Live at the Deaf Club on Manifesto Records on January 27, 2004, produced by Ray. Biafra criticized the release.

years.h: The first single: "California Über Alles", paid for with a year of gig money
years.p: Biafra and East Bay Ray started Alternative Tentacles to release it. The target was California governor Jerry Brown; the B-side was "The Man with the Dogs."

years.h: [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] finishes fourth in the San Francisco mayor's race
years.p: He collected 6,591 votes, 3.79 percent, in a ten-candidate field; Dianne Feinstein won the runoff. His slogan, borrowed from a Jell-O ad, was "There's always room for Jello."
years.xp:
Biafra says Ted put the idea in his head, telling him he had such a big mouth he should run for mayor. Per SF Weekly, he wrote his platform on a napkin at a Pere Ubu show: businessmen in clown suits inside city limits, elected neighborhood police, Pier 39 demolished, a citywide car ban, and a statue of Dan White for pelting with eggs and produce.

When Feinstein staged a street-sweeping photo op in the Tenderloin, he answered by vacuuming leaves off her lawn.

eras.title: Fresh Fruit, a swap behind the kit, and a title the BBC couldn't say
eras.text: The band's first album came out in the UK on Cherry Red, they lost their drummer to architecture school, and two singles, one about Cambodia and one about a night out, got them banned, stickered and charted.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death
years.h: At the Bammies, Biafra stops the band's own song 15 seconds in
years.p: He told the Bay Area Music Awards crowd they were a new wave band. Members wore black ties with dollar signs and played "Pull My Strings", a song mocking the music business.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the band played "Pull My Strings" only twice: once at the Bammies and once at the Mabuhay within a week, as Klaus Flouride recalled in 2017. The Bammies version was finally released on the 1987 compilation Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death.

yt: Holiday in Cambodia, official lyric video
years.h: "Holiday in Cambodia" comes out as a single, backed with "Police Truck"
years.p: It was written just after the Cambodian genocide and aimed at comfortable Western college kids; the sleeve used a photo of the Thammasat University massacre in Thailand.
years.xp: Ray told Guitar World in 2025 that the song started as a jam in the rehearsal studio, part of his case that the band wrote together. Biafra's fight with his old bandmates over this same song, and whether it would sell jeans, comes 18 years later.

years.h: Fresh Fruit for Rotting Vegetables · Cherry Red
years.p: Recorded at Möbius Music in May and June 1980. The cover is a photo from the 1979 White Night riots; Trouser Press called it a companion to the Sex Pistols' debut.

years.cap: D.H. Peligro on drums. Photo needed.
yt: Holiday in Cambodia, live at Target Video (1981)
years.h: Ted quits for architecture; [[D.H. Peligro|af1735a0-8e58-41f7-a091-03d2578e9a51]] takes over on drums
years.p: Ted, Bruce Slesinger, played his last show in February 1981. Peligro, who moved to San Francisco from St. Louis, saw the band, auditioned and got the job.

years.src: Wikipedia: Too Drunk to Fuck · Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys
years.h: "Too Drunk to Fuck" reaches No. 36, so the BBC bans it
years.p: Radio 1 wouldn't play it and chart listings printed the title as "Too Drunk To." Shops that wouldn't stock it got stickers from the band.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the stickers told buyers they were "the victim of yet another stodgy retailer" afraid to reveal the title. The single also topped the UK indie chart. Wikipedia's accounts of what presenter Tony Blackburn said on air differ slightly between pages; one has him describing it as "a record by a group calling themselves The Dead Kennedys."

years.h: "Nazi Punks Fuck Off" ships with a crossed-out swastika armband
years.p: Biafra wrote it about violent punks at shows, saying they were acting like Nazis. The free armband was later adopted by Anti-Racist Action.

years.h: In God We Trust, Inc. · the first tape peeled apart
years.p: Eight songs cut on June 19 at Subterranean Studios were lost when the tape's oxide flaked off; they redid them on August 22 at Möbius. The cover shows a gold Jesus on a cross of dollar bills.

eras.title: Faster, meaner, and busy running a label
eras.text: Peligro's first full album pushed the band toward hardcore, and then the band mostly stopped recording so Biafra and Ray could work on Alternative Tentacles.

years.h: Plastic Surgery Disasters · Thom Wilson produces
years.p: Recorded in June 1982. Peligro's first full album with the band; the cover is Michael Wells's photo of a malnourished Ugandan child. Wikipedia says it's Biafra's favorite.

years.h: Alternative Tentacles signs with distributor Mordam
years.p: The partnership began in 1983 and lasted until Mordam closed in 2009. Its owner, Ruth Schwartz, is later charged alongside Biafra in the Frankenchrist case.

years.h: No new album: the band tours and works on the label
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the band took a break from recording in 1983 and 1984 to concentrate on Alternative Tentacles.

eras.title: A poster inside the record, a raid, and a last show in Davis
eras.text: Frankenchrist shipped with a Giger painting folded inside. A complaint, a police search and criminal charges followed, and the band that had fought over everything else split up in the middle of it.

years.h: Frankenchrist · Hyde Street Studios
years.p: Biafra produced the third studio album in May and July 1985. Four Shriners pictured on the cover sued the band in 1986 over the photo, which Newsweek had published in the 1970s.

years.h: The Giger poster costs $600 and comes with a warning sticker
years.p: H.R. Giger agreed to license "Landscape XX" for $600, half his usual fee. The band vetoed it for the cover, so it went inside as a poster, with a sticker on the shrinkwrap warning of an image some might find shocking or offensive.

years.src: Diffuser · Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Jello Biafra
yt: Jello Biafra on the obscenity trial
years.h: Police search Biafra's San Francisco home for the poster
years.p: Biafra says officers took three copies of Frankenchrist, three spare posters and his private mail after a two-and-a-half-hour search.
years.xp:
The case began in December 1985, when a teenage girl bought the album at a Wherehouse in Los Angeles County; Diffuser reports she was 14 and bought it for her 11-year-old brother. Her mother wrote to the California attorney general and Los Angeles prosecutors. Biafra says the complaint traced to the Parents Music Resource Center.

In June 1986 Biafra, Alternative Tentacles manager Michael Bonanno, Mordam's Ruth Schwartz, distributor Steve Boudreau and factory owner Salvatore Alberti were charged with distributing harmful matter to minors, which carried up to a year in county jail. Charges against Schwartz, Boudreau and Alberti were dismissed for lack of evidence. Sources give the raid as April 1986; one blog says April 15.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mutiny on the Bay · Wikipedia: Bedtime for Democracy
years.h: Last show with Biafra: Freeborn Hall, Davis, California
years.p: The recording of the February 21, 1986 set later closed out the live album Mutiny on the Bay. Wikipedia says the band had decided to split in January.
years.xp: The band also played The Stone in San Francisco on February 16 and 17, and those nights appear on the same 2001 live album. Sources differ on when the split became public: the Bedtime for Democracy Wikipedia page says the breakup was announced after that album's release.

years.h: Bedtime for Democracy · a title aimed at Reagan
years.p: Recorded in April and July 1986 while the case hung over them. It opens with a cover of David Allan Coe's "Take This Job and Shove It"; the title riffs on Ronald Reagan's film Bedtime for Bonzo.

eras.title: Hung jury, and a vault of leftovers
eras.text: The band was over, but the poster case wasn't. A Los Angeles jury got the case in August 1987, and a compilation of unreleased tracks came out that summer.

years.h: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death · the odds and ends
years.p: Unreleased tracks and alternate versions from 1979 to 1987, including the Bammies performance. Wikipedia calls it the last Dead Kennedys album Biafra approved production of.
play: Give Me Convenience or Give Me Death

years.big: "Giger sees people the way Ramirez sees people."
q: Giger sees people the way Ramirez sees people.
yt: Jello Biafra interview at the trial, August 1987
years.h: Los Angeles trial ends with a jury split 7 to 5 for acquittal
years.p: Prosecutor Michael Guarino said this in court about H.R. Giger. After two days, jurors couldn't agree on Biafra and Michael Bonanno, and the judge refused a retrial.
years.xp:
Judge Susan Isacoff ruled the poster had to be judged alongside the album's music and lyrics, not on its own. The case took about 18 months to reach court. After the hung jury, Quartz reports several younger jurors asked Biafra to sign their copy of the poster, and Alternative Tentacles later sold it by mail order with age verification.

Diffuser reports Guarino later said he'd been on the wrong side of history. The legal bills nearly bankrupted Alternative Tentacles; fans helped it survive, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Biafra turns the trial into a two-disc talk: High Priest of Harmful Matter
years.p: The 1989 spoken-word album puts a censorship lecture on disc one and "Tales from the Trial" on disc two.

eras.title: Ray, Flouride and Peligro v. Biafra
eras.text: The three musicians who'd outvoted Jello Biafra on the catalog took him to court over unpaid royalties. Biafra says it was punishment for refusing a jeans ad. The band says it was about money. A jury and an appeals court sided with the band.

years.src: Justia · Snopes · The Moscow Times · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles
years.h: Ray, Flouride and Peligro vote Alternative Tentacles out as catalog administrator
years.p: Decay Music, the four members' partnership since 1981, is the owner of the songs. Biafra withheld royalties pending court approval, and the three sued in October 1998 for about $76,000 in unpaid royalties.
years.xp:
Their claims, per Snopes and Wikipedia: Biafra conspired to pay lower royalty rates and hid what was owed, raised retail prices without raising the royalty calculation, and failed to promote the old catalog. In a 1999 ruling, a federal judge sent the case back to state court, finding the partnership claims weren't a copyright matter.

Biafra's side: Alternative Tentacles found an accounting error and corrected it before the suit. Ray's side: "He was picking money that was supposed to go to the Dead Kennedys and spending it on himself." Wikipedia also says Ray sold his stake in the label in the mid-1980s over "personal, financial and philosophical differences."

q: We tried our darndest to settle it.
years.src: NME · Deseret News · The Moscow Times · Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles
years.h: San Francisco jury: Biafra owes his old band about $220,000
years.p: That was the jury's finding against Biafra and Alternative Tentacles, per Wikipedia. It also decided that Decay Music, not individual songwriters, owned the songs.
years.xp:
Biafra told the San Francisco Chronicle it was "the ugliest thing that's ever happened to me" and, per NME, that the band was punishing him for sticking to the band's principles. He said he'd consider an appeal.

The bandmates said they'd tried to settle. Wikipedia says the initial underpayment was an accounting error but the jury found he'd withheld information during negotiations. Reported totals vary between about $200,000 and $220,000; The Moscow Times says he'd also receive no royalties until paying the three another $140,000.

years.h: Biafra says it was about a Levi's ad; the band says that never happened
years.p: Biafra's account: the suit is payback for refusing to let "Holiday in Cambodia" sell Dockers. The band's answer: no such request existed.
years.xp:
Biafra told PopMatters an ad agency proposed the song for a Dockers commercial, that he refused over Levi's layoffs and executive pay, and that the ad ran with a Pretenders song instead. He told another interviewer Ray asked, "Why don't you just go to the press and tell them we did it for charity?"

The band consistently denied it and called it a smokescreen; its lawyer, David Given, said the band "weren't down with it, and it never happened." Snopes rates the claim unproven, since neither jury nor judge ruled on what started the fight.

years.h: Mutiny on the Bay · the first post-verdict live album
years.p: Manifesto Records issued live sets from 1982 and 1986, including the last show with Biafra. Biafra criticized the release and later said he asked them to take his name off a live album.

years.h: Ray, Flouride and Peligro re-form Dead Kennedys with Brandon Cruz
years.p: Cruz, formerly of Dr. Know, sang from 2001 until May 2003. Biafra dismissed the new lineup as the world's greediest karaoke band.
years.xp: Flouride said in 2003 there hadn't been a show yet that people didn't really like. Biafra told PopMatters that Flouride was seen onstage in San Francisco saying they'd rehearsed only twice in thirteen years. In a 2012 Tampa Bay Times interview, Biafra said: "We haven't talked in a dozen years."

years.src: Wikipedia: Alternative Tentacles · Wikipedia: Jello Biafra · PopMatters
years.h: Appeals court upholds the verdict, and the catalog goes to Decay Music
years.p: Biafra had to pay the outstanding royalties plus punitive damages and hand the majority of the back catalog to Decay Music.
years.xp: Manifesto Records became the US licensee of the Dead Kennedys albums. Biafra described losing the catalog as "like getting some of your limbs blown off," per Wikipedia. His side: he said the ex-bandmates "never had to get jobs" while he kept the records in print for 22 years.

eras.title: Whose band is it now
eras.text: The reunited band has toured for two decades with three different singers, and licenses songs to films and games. Biafra objects to nearly all of it. Nobody has budged.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dead Kennedys · Wikipedia: Too Drunk to Fuck
years.h: The Manchurian Candidate remake and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater license songs
years.p: Ray, Flouride and Peligro licensed tracks to the 2004 film and to the video game, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Ray says he received a fax from Alternative Tentacles indicating Biafra approved the game license. Biafra said of a later license, a Nouvelle Vague cover used in a 2007 scene of Robert Rodriguez's Planet Terror, that it went against everything the band stood for. The band told him to donate his share of the money to charity.

years.h: Jeff Penalty leaves; Ron "Skip" Greer becomes the singer
years.p: Penalty replaced Cruz in May 2003. Greer, formerly of the Wynona Riders, has fronted the band since.

years.h: Riot Fest asks about a Biafra reunion; Ray says he'd play, Biafra won't
years.p: Ray said in 2017 that Riot Fest approached the band and he and Klaus Flouride were interested.
years.xp: Ray repeated the claim in a May 2025 Guitar World interview: "It's Biafra that turns down any offers." He also said Biafra "got caught with his hands in the till and wants to blame us for getting caught." On songwriting he said the band wrote together and the chemistry made two plus two equal five. Biafra has said a reunion for nostalgia would go against what punk stands for.

years.h: D.H. Peligro dies in Los Angeles at 63
years.p: An autopsy released May 2, 2023 found the combined effects of fentanyl and heroin, with non-small cell lung cancer present, not the head trauma first reported.
